# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project state

Mon1e is a Foundry VTT **v14** Game System for the tabletop RPG "Mon" (Fringe Worlds). The repo is currently a scaffold only: `package.json` (no dependencies), a placeholder `index.js`, and the framing brief. There is no `system.json` and no `src/` yet.

Current work: GitHub issue #1, "Milestone 1 - Mon1e Bootstrap (0.0.1)". Foundry recognizes the system, a test world starts, and Git plus basic checks work. No rules engine. It covers P0-P2 of the brief.

Source of truth for stack and roadmap (in French): `documentation/cadrage/bootstrap/bootstraping-initial-project.md`. Read it before planning work.

## Commands

No working commands exist yet. `npm test` is the default placeholder and exits 1. Planned in the brief, not yet created:

- `npm run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit` with `allowJs` + `checkJs`
- `npm test`: Node.js `node:test`
- `npm run check`: runs all technical checks

Once tests exist, run a single file with `node --test tests/<file>.test.mjs`.

## Target architecture

- Native Game System: JavaScript ES Modules (`.mjs`), JSDoc + `checkJs`, `TypeDataModel` for data, `ApplicationV2` + Handlebars for sheets. No build step, bundler, React/Vite/Docker, or other framework until a concrete need appears. `typescript` is a dev dependency only for `checkJs`; never write `.ts` files.
- Manifest `system.json`: id `mon1e`, type `system`, compatibility minimum/verified 14, esmodules `src/main.mjs`. The entry point registers components on the `init` hook.
- Indicative layout, not an obligation: `src/{models,rules,sheets,foundry}`, `templates/`, `styles/`, `lang/`, `tests/`, `docs/{RULES,DECISIONS,DEVELOPMENT}.md`. Create only what the next feature needs.
- Keep the rules engine (`src/rules`) free of Foundry dependencies so pure game logic is unit-testable with `node:test`. Test Foundry integration in the real runtime. `checkJs` does not cover Foundry APIs, so state its actual coverage honestly.
- The brief expects the repo to live in `<User Data>/Data/systems/mon1e/` so Foundry picks up edits without copying.

## Working rules

- Never invent or silently change a Mon rule. Confirmed rules and unknowns belong in `docs/RULES.md`. Data types (Actor/Item) are chosen only after the rules are confirmed.
- Check Foundry v14 APIs against the official docs before using them.
- Build in vertical slices, one feature at a time. A feature is done only when its behavior is verified and its data persists after reloading the world.

### Configuration and Persistence

- Make these conventions persistent using the configuration mechanism supported by the installed tools.
- Verify the expected configuration schema before creating or modifying any configuration file.
- Do not assume the structure of `.llm-workbench/project.json` without validating it first.
- Create `documentation/plans/` if it does not already exist.
- Check for existing files, naming collisions, and duplicate plans before creating a new plan.
- Never overwrite an existing plan without explicit approval.

### Plan Generation

Generate the implementation plan using:

```text
/plan-from-issue https://github.com/behaska/foundryvtt-mon1e/issues/1
```

The plan must:

- Be written in French.
- Follow the planning conventions defined above.
- Be limited to phases **P0, P1, and P2** of `documentation/cadrage/bootstrap/bootstraping-initial-project.md`.
- Respect the existing project architecture, technical decisions, and documented requirements.
- Avoid introducing undocumented features, unnecessary abstractions, or additional scope.
- Define actionable implementation steps, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and expected validation procedures.
- Remain a planning artifact only: do not implement code, modify GitHub issues, run tests, or create commits or pull requests.

### Expected Output

The expected plan location is:

```text
documentation/plans/issue-1-mon1e-bootstrap.md
```

Verify the actual issue title and generate the filename according to the configured naming convention.

Report the exact created file path upon successful completion. If any required information or configuration is missing, report the blocker explicitly instead of making assumptions.
